stem.en: Which statement correctly compares the cell wall and the cell membrane?

text.en: The wall is selectively permeable, and the membrane is freely permeable.

feedback.en: This has the two the wrong way round.

text.en: Both are rigid layers that let nothing pass through them.

feedback.en: The membrane is fluid, and the wall lets most substances pass.

text.en: The wall is permeable; the membrane is selective.

feedback.en: Yes. The membrane controls what crosses, and the wall gives rigidity.

text.en: Both are found in every animal cell and every plant cell.

feedback.en: Animal cells have no cell wall.

explanation.en: The cell wall is permeable and rigid. The cell membrane is selectively permeable, so it is the membrane that controls what enters and leaves.

hints.en: Which layer controls what enters the cell?
